title: Kloni — Mind mapping for macOS, with tasks built in
excerpt: Keyboard-first, local-first mind mapping for macOS, with tasks baked in.
content_html:
Kloni Get Kloni

Kloni — mind mapping for macOS. Think it through.
See it through.

Keyboard-first, local-first mind mapping for macOS,
with tasks baked in.
Assign dates, statuses, and priorities to every node.
The same map can hold your first thought
and your final task.

Mind maps have always been a place for thinking. is also a place for doing.

The same node you sketched as an idea can become the task you mark done.

The thinking surfaces

Two views,
one thought.

A canvas for spatial thinking. An outline for sequential thinking. The same underlying data stays in sync between them.

Write straight into the outline — indent with Tab, add the next line with Enter, fold any branch — then arrange it on the canvas. Or sketch branches loosely and read them back as a document. Whichever lens fits the moment.

Outline

Canvas

Beneath the label

Every node
has depth.

A label is just the entry point.
Underneath, every node can carry rich text, attachments, and links out to other maps in your library.

Rich notes.

Open an intuitive rich text editor on any node. Type / for slash commands, or select text for a formatting bubble. Images, tables, code blocks — all live, all inside the bundle so it travels together.

Inline images.

Drop an image onto a node and it renders right on the canvas. Mockups, references, sketches — visible as part of the map.

Three node types.

Default for ideas. Checkbox for tasks, with cascading completion that propagates up and down the tree. Link to attach a URL, openable in one keystroke.

Inter-map links.

Link a node to another map — or to a specific node inside it. The kloni:// protocol resolves by stable ID, so links survive a rename. Broken links flag themselves.

Cross-links.

Connect any two nodes with a labeled arc. One-directional or bi-directional, color-coded, smart-routed. For relationships the tree can't express.

File attachments.

Drop images, PDFs, anything — files live inside the map bundle, not scattered across your disk. Forty-plus file types with type-specific icons. Nothing lost on copy.

Properties

Any node,
a task.

Tick a checkbox. Set a date. Mark a status. Flag a priority. Any one of them turns a node into a task — without changing what a mind map fundamentally is. Type a date in plain words — tomorrow, next Friday — or pick the calendar, and set it all from the keyboard with /date and /priority.

Four signals, every node, optional everywhere. The branch you sketched as a half-thought yesterday is the task you mark done tomorrow — in the same map, with no conversion, no migration, no second app.

Tasks

Today, inbox,
blocked.

Three views surface what's actionable across your whole library. Today — what's due, overdue, or in progress. Inbox — what you've captured but haven't triaged. Blocked — what's waiting on something.

Action-first. Tap a status to cycle it, a checkbox to complete, a node's label to jump to its map. Even checkboxes tucked inside a node's note show up in Inbox, ready to toggle or promote — fast capture without losing the workflow.

Layouts

Nine ways
to see the same map.

Layout is a rendering decision, not a data decision.
The same map can be a tree for brainstorming, a table for comparison, and a Kanban board for execution — without losing a node, a note, or a tag.

Switch freely. Find the shape that matches the thought.

Right Tree

The classic. Root on the left, branches growing right.

Top Tree

Root at the top-left, first child beside it, the rest flowing down.

Top Down

Vertical org-chart. Root at top, children fanning out below.

Balanced

Root at center, branches distributed symmetrically on both sides.

Tree List

A dense, file-explorer style for deep hierarchies.

Timeline

Horizontal spine. Milestones alternate above and below.

Ishikawa

Cause-and-effect fishbone. Recursive, for root-cause analysis.

Tree Table

A grid. Rows and columns for tabular visualization.

Columns

Top-level children as headers. Ideal for Kanban and comparison.

Spaces

One library,
many contexts.

Group maps into spaces — Work, Reading, Side Projects — and the library becomes organized instead of a flat pile. Maps stay maps; spaces stay light. No nesting, no per-space settings, no slow accretion into "projects with their own everything."

Spaces aren't just folders — they're a scope. Tasks, library exploration, search results all narrow to the active space. Open Today inside Work and you see this week's work; switch to Personal and you see your reading. One scope, every view.

History

Rewind
any map.

Every edit — a moved branch, a status change, a rewritten note — flows into a per-map history you can step through and restore from. Open the timeline (⌘⇧H) and scrub: day-grouped entries, plain-language summaries, before-and-after diffs on each node.

Undo goes 250 steps deep and behaves the same on the canvas, in the outline view, and inside a note. The whole history lives in the map's bundle — it travels with the file, with no server keeping score.

Private by default

Your thoughts and your tasks
go only where you take them.

• No cloud.

• No sync server.

• No account.

Every map lives on your disk as a bundle you can move, back up, or version – with any tool you already trust.

Quick capture

One hotkey,
from anywhere.

A global keyboard shortcut summons a small capture window from anywhere on your Mac. Type the idea or the task, hit return, and it lands in your designated map. Or click the menu bar icon when your hands are on the trackpad.

Need more than a label? Press tab and the window expands into a full rich text editor — the same rich notes, file attachments, and node depth as the rest of Kloni. Capture small, grow when you're ready.

Compact

Expanded

Command palette

Every command,
at your fingertips.

A single shortcut opens a fuzzy-search palette over every action Kloni knows — switch layouts, jump to a tagged node, mark a node done, run a template, anything. Type a few letters, hit return.

Memorize shortcuts for what you do every day. Use the palette for everything else. Both habits live in the same hand position; nothing requires reaching for the mouse.

And to move between maps, Quick Open (⌘⇧O): type a few letters, hit return, and you're in the map you wanted — switching to its open tab if there is one, loading it if not.

Tags

Tag, filter,
discover.

Tag any node, anywhere. Filter by one tag or many.
Click a tag on the canvas and every node that carries it lights up.

Tags travel with the map but also live library-wide — browse every tag across every map, with counts, in a single panel. Not just labels: filter Tasks by tag, scope Search by tag, narrow any library query.

research ideas decisions deep-work product go-to-market

Search

Search across
every map.

Find a phrase or a note — in the map you're in, in a space, or anywhere in your library. Relevance-scored matches in labels, notes, and breadcrumb paths.

Open with a keystroke. Narrow by tag, status, or date. Hit return on any result, and the map opens with the matched node already in focus — not just opened, located.

Templates

Start from
somewhere.

Twelve starting points that pair a structure with the layout that flatters it. A SWOT that knows it wants to be balanced, a weekly review pre-shaped for reflection, a Kanban that opens straight into columns.

Half are productivity workflows ready to run. The rest are thinking structures ready to fill. Either way, the layout's already chosen and the bones are in place — start with the work, not the setup.

Balanced

SWOT Analysis

Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats.

Timeline

Project Plan

Phases, tasks, milestones on a spine.

Tree List

Meeting Notes

Agenda, discussion, decisions, actions.

Balanced

Weekly Review

Last week's recap, next week's plan.

Ishikawa

Problem Analysis

Root cause analysis with fishbone.

Tree List

Book Outline

Parts, chapters, sections.

Tree Table

Decision Review

Compare options against criteria.

Columns

Kanban Board

To do, in progress, done.

Columns

Pros & Cons

Weigh arguments for and against.

Top Down

Org Chart

Team structure and roles.

Right Tree

Feature Map

Product features and capabilities.

Top Tree

Learning Roadmap

Skills, topics, study paths.

Appearance

Dark, light,
or automatic.

Twelve color themes. Light and dark modes, or follow the system. Node shape, fill style, edge curvature, density — all configurable. Custom colors per node when you want them.

A frosted-glass toolbar that knows which mode it's in.

Light

Dark

Pricing

One-time
purchase.

Introductory Price

$35

($50 Full price)

Price in USD — varies by region on the App Store

Pay once. Own it.

No subscription, no cloud fees.

Works offline. Always.

Most problems in life occur for two reasons:
we act without thinking
or we keep thinking without acting.

Keep thinking.
Keep doing.

Download on the Mac App Store

Universal binary — Apple Silicon & Intel

content_html_zh:
Kloni Get Kloni

Kloni — mind mapping for macOS. Think it through.See it through.

Keyboard-first, local-first mind mapping for macOS, with tasks baked in. Assign dates, statuses, and priorities to every node. The same map can hold your first thought and your final task.

Mind maps have always been a place for thinking. is also a place for doing.

The same node you sketched as an idea can become the task you mark done.

The thinking surfaces

Two views,one thought.

A canvas for spatial thinking. An outline for sequential thinking. The same underlying data stays in sync between them.

Write straight into the outline — indent with Tab, add the next line with Enter, fold any branch — then arrange it on the canvas. Or sketch branches loosely and read them back as a document. Whichever lens fits the moment.

大纲

帆布

Beneath the label

Every nodehas depth.

A label is just the entry point. Underneath, every node can carry rich text, attachments, and links out to other maps in your library.

Rich notes.

Open an intuitive rich text editor on any node. Type / for slash commands, or select text for a formatting bubble. Images, tables, code blocks — all live, all inside the bundle so it travels together.

Inline images.

Drop an image onto a node and it renders right on the canvas. Mockups, references, sketches — visible as part of the map.

Three node types.

Default for ideas. Checkbox for tasks, with cascading completion that propagates up and down the tree. Link to attach a URL, openable in one keystroke.

Inter-map links.

Link a node to another map — or to a specific node inside it. The kloni:// protocol resolves by stable ID, so links survive a rename. Broken links flag themselves.

Cross-links.

Connect any two nodes with a labeled arc. One-directional or bi-directional, color-coded, smart-routed. For relationships the tree can't express.

File attachments.

Drop images, PDFs, anything — files live inside the map bundle, not scattered across your disk. Forty-plus file types with type-specific icons. Nothing lost on copy.

特性

Any node,a task.

Tick a checkbox. Set a date. Mark a status. Flag a priority. Any one of them turns a node into a task — without changing what a mind map fundamentally is. Type a date in plain words — tomorrow, next Friday — or pick the calendar, and set it all from the keyboard with /date and /priority.

Four signals, every node, optional everywhere. The branch you sketched as a half-thought yesterday is the task you mark done tomorrow — in the same map, with no conversion, no migration, no second app.

Tasks

Today, inbox,blocked.

Three views surface what's actionable across your whole library. Today — what's due, overdue, or in progress. Inbox — what you've captured but haven't triaged. Blocked — what's waiting on something.

Action-first. Tap a status to cycle it, a checkbox to complete, a node's label to jump to its map. Even checkboxes tucked inside a node's note show up in Inbox, ready to toggle or promote — fast capture without losing the workflow.

Layouts

Nine ways to see the same map.

Layout is a rendering decision, not a data decision. The same map can be a tree for brainstorming, a table for comparison, and a Kanban board for execution — without losing a node, a note, or a tag.

Switch freely. Find the shape that matches the thought.

Right Tree

经典。 Root on the left, branches growing right.

Top Tree

Root at the top-left, first child beside it, the rest flowing down.

Top Down

Vertical org-chart. Root at top, children fanning out below.

均衡

Root at center, branches distributed symmetrically on both sides.

Tree List

A dense, file-explorer style for deep hierarchies.

时间轴

Horizontal spine. Milestones alternate above and below.

Ishikawa

Cause-and-effect fishbone. Recursive, for root-cause analysis.

Tree Table

A grid. Rows and columns for tabular visualization.

专栏

Top-level children as headers. Ideal for Kanban and comparison.

空间

One library,many contexts.

Group maps into spaces — Work, Reading, Side Projects — and the library becomes organized instead of a flat pile. Maps stay maps; spaces stay light. No nesting, no per-space settings, no slow accretion into "projects with their own everything."

Spaces aren't just folders — they're a scope. Tasks, library exploration, search results all narrow to the active space. Open Today inside Work and you see this week's work; switch to Personal and you see your reading. One scope, every view.

历史

Rewindany map.

Every edit — a moved branch, a status change, a rewritten note — flows into a per-map history you can step through and restore from. Open the timeline (⌘⇧H) and scrub: day-grouped entries, plain-language summaries, before-and-after diffs on each node.

Undo goes 250 steps deep and behaves the same on the canvas, in the outline view, and inside a note. The whole history lives in the map's bundle — it travels with the file, with no server keeping score.

默认为私有

Your thoughts and your tasks go only where you take them.

• No cloud.

• No sync server.

• No account.

Every map lives on your disk as a bundle you can move, back up, or version – with any tool you already trust.

快速捕捉

One hotkey,from anywhere.

A global keyboard shortcut summons a small capture window from anywhere on your Mac. Type the idea or the task, hit return, and it lands in your designated map. Or click the menu bar icon when your hands are on the trackpad.

Need more than a label? Press tab and the window expands into a full rich text editor — the same rich notes, file attachments, and node depth as the rest of Kloni. Capture small, grow when you're ready.

Compact

扩展

Command palette

Every command,at your fingertips.

A single shortcut opens a fuzzy-search palette over every action Kloni knows — switch layouts, jump to a tagged node, mark a node done, run a template, anything. Type a few letters, hit return.

Memorize shortcuts for what you do every day. Use the palette for everything else. Both habits live in the same hand position; nothing requires reaching for the mouse.

And to move between maps, Quick Open (⌘⇧O): type a few letters, hit return, and you're in the map you wanted — switching to its open tab if there is one, loading it if not.

Tags

Tag, filter,discover.

Tag any node, anywhere. Filter by one tag or many. Click a tag on the canvas and every node that carries it lights up.

Tags travel with the map but also live library-wide — browse every tag across every map, with counts, in a single panel. Not just labels: filter Tasks by tag, scope Search by tag, narrow any library query.

research ideas decisions deep-work product go-to-market

搜索

Search acrossevery map.

Find a phrase or a note — in the map you're in, in a space, or anywhere in your library. Relevance-scored matches in labels, notes, and breadcrumb paths.

Open with a keystroke. Narrow by tag, status, or date. Hit return on any result, and the map opens with the matched node already in focus — not just opened, located.

模板

Start fromsomewhere.

Twelve starting points that pair a structure with the layout that flatters it. A SWOT that knows it wants to be balanced, a weekly review pre-shaped for reflection, a Kanban that opens straight into columns.

Half are productivity workflows ready to run. The rest are thinking structures ready to fill. Either way, the layout's already chosen and the bones are in place — start with the work, not the setup.
